title: Summative Test 2 — Life Science & Organ Systems
revision: 2026-11 rev2 — 70:30 LOTS:HOTS, balanced choices, in-scope items only

questions.text: What does cell theory state?
options: All living things are made of cells
All cells are made of living organs
Only animals are made of many cells
Cells form from non-living matter
questions.correct: All living things are made of cells

questions.text: A group of similar cells working together forms a…
options: Tissue
Organ
Organism
Organ system
questions.correct: Tissue

questions.text: Why are red blood cells shaped like flattened discs with a dent?
options: More surface and room for carrying oxygen
To store DNA in a much larger nucleus
To make blood thicker and flow slowly
To produce hormones for body heat control
questions.correct: More surface and room for carrying oxygen

questions.text: Why do villi line the small intestine?
options: They increase the area for absorbing food
They push food back up into the stomach
They produce bile to break down the fats
They store air for the lungs to use later
questions.correct: They increase the area for absorbing food

questions.text: Bees pollinate flowers while flowers give bees nectar. Which theme of life is this?
options: Interdependence
Homeostasis
Heredity
Cell theory of life
questions.correct: Interdependence

questions.text: A plant's roots are damaged by a flood, and its leaves wilt within days. Which idea BEST explains this?
options: Parts of a system depend on each other
Leaves and roots work completely alone
Flood water poisons only the leaves
Roots make food that leaves need
questions.correct: Parts of a system depend on each other

questions.text: Which comparison BEST shows that an organ can do what single cells cannot?
options: The heart pumps blood; one heart cell cannot
One muscle cell can lift a whole sack of rice
A tissue is always larger than a full organ
Cells and organs have exactly the same jobs
questions.correct: The heart pumps blood; one heart cell cannot

questions.text: You must diagram structure and function in a leaf. Which pair of labels is MOST accurate?
options: Flat, wide blade → captures more light
Thick bark layer → absorbs water from soil
Root hairs on the leaf → store sugar
Hard shell → protects seeds from rain
questions.correct: Flat, wide blade → captures more light

questions.text: Which structure controls what enters and leaves the cell?
options: Cell membrane
Cell wall (plants)
Nucleus
Vacuole
questions.correct: Cell membrane

questions.text: Which organelle contains the cell's DNA in plants and animals?
options: Nucleus
Ribosome
Vacuole
Mitochondrion
questions.correct: Nucleus

questions.text: How does oxygen enter a cell from the blood?
options: By diffusion from high to low concentration
By active transport using a lot of ATP
By osmosis together with water molecules
By endocytosis inside large membrane pockets
questions.correct: By diffusion from high to low concentration

questions.text: How do white blood cells take in whole bacteria?
options: Endocytosis — the membrane wraps around them
Osmosis — water carries them through pores
Diffusion — they slip through tiny gaps
Photosynthesis — they turn them into simple sugar
questions.correct: Endocytosis — the membrane wraps around them

questions.text: Which stage of respiration happens in the cytoplasm and needs no oxygen?
options: Glycolysis
Krebs cycle
Electron transport
Photosynthesis
questions.correct: Glycolysis

questions.text: What are the products of anaerobic respiration in human muscles?
options: Lactic acid and a little ATP
Alcohol and carbon dioxide gas
Glucose and oxygen gas
Water and a lot of ATP
questions.correct: Lactic acid and a little ATP

questions.text: Cucumber slices are soaked in salty vinegar for atchara and become limp. What happened?
options: Water left the cucumber cells by osmosis
Salt entered and made the cells swell
Vinegar added more water into the cucumber
Heat in the jar cooked the cucumber
questions.correct: Water left the cucumber cells by osmosis

questions.text: A person with anemia has too little hemoglobin. Which effect on their cells is MOST likely?
options: Less oxygen arrives, so less ATP is made
More glucose enters every cell at once
Cells switch to doing photosynthesis
Mitochondria start making their own hemoglobin
questions.correct: Less oxygen arrives, so less ATP is made

questions.text: Which tissue carries water and minerals from roots to leaves?
options: Xylem
Phloem
Epidermis
Cuticle
questions.correct: Xylem

questions.text: What are stomata?
options: Pores on leaves for gas exchange
Tubes that carry sugar downward
Hairs on roots that take in water
Cells that store starch in roots
questions.correct: Pores on leaves for gas exchange

questions.text: In plant transport, which part is usually a SOURCE of sugar?
options: Mature leaves
Growing fruits
Storage roots
New flower buds
questions.correct: Mature leaves

questions.text: Which condition speeds up transpiration the MOST?
options: Hot, dry and windy weather
Cool, humid and still air
Night time with no sunlight
Rainy days with full clouds
questions.correct: Hot, dry and windy weather

questions.text: Why does wood make up most of a tree trunk?
options: Old xylem builds up and supports the tree
Phloem hardens into wood every season
Leaves fall and are stored inside the trunk
Roots grow upward and fill the trunk
questions.correct: Old xylem builds up and supports the tree

questions.text: Celery is placed in red-colored water. After a day, red lines appear in its stalk. What do these lines show?
options: The xylem carried water up the stalk
The phloem carried sugar to the roots
The stomata absorbed the colored water
The leaves made the red color by themselves
questions.correct: The xylem carried water up the stalk

questions.text: A kamote plant's leaves are all eaten by pests, and its storage roots stop growing. Which explanation BEST links the organs?
options: Without leaves, no sugar is made and sent to the roots
Without leaves, the roots absorb too much water
Without leaves, the xylem carries sugar upward
Without leaves, the roots start photosynthesizing underground
questions.correct: Without leaves, no sugar is made and sent to the roots

questions.text: When body temperature rises, what does the hypothalamus trigger?
options: Sweating and widening of skin blood vessels
Shivering and narrowing of blood vessels
More thyroid hormone to raise metabolism
Goosebumps to trap warm air near the skin surface
questions.correct: Sweating and widening of skin blood vessels

questions.text: Which is part of the FIRST line of defense?
options: Skin and mucus
Antibodies
Memory B cells
Fever
questions.correct: Skin and mucus

questions.text: What do memory cells do?
options: Respond quickly if the same germ returns
Store food energy for the whole immune system
Carry oxygen to the lymph nodes
Make the skin thicker against germs
questions.correct: Respond quickly if the same germ returns

questions.text: Which describes a torn ACL?
options: A damaged knee ligament that makes the knee unstable
A broken arm bone that heals by itself within a few days
A lung infection that causes heavy coughing
A burst blood vessel in the brain during sleep
questions.correct: A damaged knee ligament that makes the knee unstable

questions.text: Why does the body use BOTH nerves and hormones to control temperature?
options: Nerves act fast; hormones give longer-lasting control
Hormones act fast; nerves give longer-lasting control
Each system works only during one time of day
Both systems do exactly the same thing at once
questions.correct: Nerves act fast; hormones give longer-lasting control

questions.text: After a measles outbreak, unvaccinated children got sick far more than vaccinated ones. What is the BEST conclusion?
options: The vaccine helped build protective immunity
Measles only infects children who do not eat
Vaccinated children were never exposed at all
The vaccine itself caused the measles outbreak
questions.correct: The vaccine helped build protective immunity

questions.text: A parent says, "My child is healthy, so vaccines are unnecessary." Which response is MOST scientifically sound?
options: Healthy kids can still catch serious diseases; vaccines prevent this
Healthy children never catch diseases, so the parent is correct
Vaccines are only useful after a child is already very sick in bed
Vaccines work only for adults, so the parent is correct
questions.correct: Healthy kids can still catch serious diseases; vaccines prevent this
